samples.question: A register of four bit-cells is shown on the left, read left to right as slot 0, 1, 2, 3. Each cell is a disk that is either FILLED (a solid disk) or HOLLOW (an outline ring). An orange ring surrounds exactly one cell and marks the TARGET cell you must track. To the right, operator glyphs are read left to right: a green right-pointing triangle rotates the whole four-bit word one step to the right (the rightmost bit wraps around to the leftmost), and a red left-pointing triangle rotates it one step to the left (the leftmost bit wraps around to the rightmost). The register is never shown again, so apply the rotations in order from the marked start. What is the final state of the ringed cell? Answer 'filled' or 'outline'.
